questions.problem:
$$
U=[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 & 0 \\ \frac{1}{\sqrt{10}} & 0 & -\frac{3}{\sqrt{10}} \\ \frac{3}{\sqrt{10}} & 0 & \frac{1}{\sqrt{10}}\end{aligned}],\,Σ=[\begin{aligned}2\sqrt{5} & 0 \\ 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}],\,V=[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} & -\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \\ \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} & \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrices shown above. Given that $A=UΣ{V}^{T}$ is a singular value decomposition of $A,$ find the pseudoinverse ${A}^{+}.$
questions.worked_solution:
If $A=UΣ{V}^{T}$ is a singular value decomposition of $A,$ then the pseudoinverse of $A$ is given by

$$
V\,{Σ}^{+}\,{U}^{T},
$$

where ${Σ}^{+}$ is the pseudoinverse of $Σ.$

First, notice that

$$
V=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}],\,{Σ}^{+}=\frac{1}{2\sqrt{5}}[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}],\,{U}^{T}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{10}}[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 & 3 \\ \sqrt{10} & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & -3 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{+} & =V\,{Σ}^{+}\,{U}^{T} \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot \frac{1}{2\sqrt{5}}[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{10}}[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 & 3 \\ \sqrt{10} & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & -3 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{20}[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}0 & 1 & 3 \\ \sqrt{10} & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & -3 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{20}[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}0 & 1 & 3 \\ \sqrt{10} & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & -3 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{20}[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 & 3 \\ 0 & 1 & 3\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

$$

Consider the matrices shown above. Given that $A=UΣ{V}^{T}$ is a singular value decomposition of $A,$ find the pseudoinverse ${A}^{+}.$
questions.worked_solution:
If $A=UΣ{V}^{T}$ is a singular value decomposition of $A,$ then the pseudoinverse of $A$ is given by

$$
V\,{Σ}^{+}\,{U}^{T},
$$

where ${Σ}^{+}$ is the pseudoinverse of $Σ.$

First, notice that

$$
{Σ}^{+}=\frac{1}{10}[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}],\,{U}^{T}=\frac{1}{5}[\begin{aligned}3 & 4 & 0 \\ -4 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 5\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{+} & =V\,{Σ}^{+}\,{U}^{T} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot \frac{1}{10}[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\cdot \frac{1}{5}[\begin{aligned}3 & 4 & 0 \\ -4 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 5\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{50}[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}3 & 4 & 0 \\ -4 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 5\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{50}[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}3 & 4 & 0 \\ -4 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 5\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{50}[\begin{aligned}3 & 4 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

$$

Consider the matrices shown above. Given that $A={U}_{r}{Σ}_{r}{V}_{r}^{T}$ is a reduced singular value decomposition of $A,$ find the pseudoinverse ${A}^{+}.$
questions.worked_solution:
If $A={U}_{r}{Σ}_{r}{V}_{r}^{T}$ is a reduced singular value decomposition of $A,$ then the pseudoinverse of $A$ is given by

$$
{V}_{r}\,{Σ}_{r}^{+}\,{U}_{r}^{T},
$$

where ${Σ}_{r}^{+}$ is the pseudoinverse of ${Σ}_{r}.$

First, notice that

$$
{Σ}_{r}^{+}=\frac{1}{5}[\begin{aligned}1\end{aligned}],\,{U}_{r}^{T}=\frac{1}{5}[\begin{aligned}4 & 3 & 0\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{+} & ={V}_{r}\,{Σ}_{r}^{+}\,{U}_{r}^{T} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]\cdot \frac{1}{5}[\begin{aligned}1\end{aligned}]\cdot \frac{1}{5}[\begin{aligned}4 & 3 & 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{25}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}4 & 3 & 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{25}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}4 & 3 & 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{25}[\begin{aligned}4 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

questions.worked_solution:
If $A={U}_{r}{Σ}_{r}{V}_{r}^{T}$ is a reduced singular value decomposition of $A,$ then the pseudoinverse of $A$ is given by

$$
{V}_{r}\,{Σ}_{r}^{+}\,{U}_{r}^{T},
$$

where ${Σ}_{r}^{+}$ is the pseudoinverse of ${Σ}_{r}.$

First, notice that

$$
{V}_{r}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{10}}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 3\end{aligned}],\,{Σ}_{r}^{+}=\frac{1}{2\sqrt{5}}[\begin{aligned}1\end{aligned}],\,{U}_{r}^{T}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}[\begin{aligned}1 & -1\end{aligned}].
$$

 

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{+} & ={V}_{r}\,{Σ}_{r}^{+}\,{U}_{r}^{T} \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{10}}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 3\end{aligned}]\cdot \frac{1}{2\sqrt{5}}[\begin{aligned}1\end{aligned}]\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}[\begin{aligned}1 & -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{20}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 3\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 & -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{20}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 3\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 & -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{20}[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 3 & -3\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
